title: Clyde Kerr Sr. and Henry Hardin
summary: Kerr as arranger, teacher and section player rather than soloist; Hardin's band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. So you've had, you've had one of those run-ins with the union. I've got some other questions. Did you know Clyde Kerr?
Could you tell me something about Clyde Kerr, senior?
Yeah, he was a good writer. He wrote arrangements. Well he had a band, he had a good band. Now his band used to play at the Tick Tock too. He was a Tick Tock band. And he had a good band.
What about him as an educator?
Yeah, well he taught music, I mean he taught at Booker T. Washington School. Then he taught at some other schools around here.
I think Xavier Prepp for him.
Yeah, yeah, he was at Xavier Prepp.
There's another guy who had a good band. Right, yeah. He had a very good band. A guy named Henry Hardin had a band too.
His band used to play at the rhythm club too. Hardin? H-A-R-D-I-N? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Were you first friends with Claude Kerr? Well we just, you know, we had a good band. Yeah.

We used to talk a lot. And he always wanted to get a band together. And have a band. We were friends with Claude Kerr. I remember Henry Hardin had a band too. His band used to play at the rhythm club too.
Hardin, H-A-R-D-I-N? Yeah. Were you first of friends with Clyde Kerr?

Well, we used to talk a lot. And he always wanted to get a band together and have Dave Bartholomew himself and me, for the three trumpet players. But he never did get it together. Because I always had my band and Dave had his band. Right. But Clyde, he wasn't a jazz player. Anything that you write down, he can play it. But I mean just to sit down and play one of those jobs on Bourbon Street. Right. Or you have to improvise. He never did have jobs like that.
Writing and playing with the section, playing parts, written parts.
